bull_bear.body: Primary allocation to clinic expansion (Omni deployment); Secondary to R&D for new products (noise protection, newborn screening); Potential M&A via Turtle Marks LLP; No dividend or buyback mentioned; No debt-funded expansion indicated
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Regulatory delays in U.S./Australia approvals; Slow adoption in rural areas despite tech; Competitor imitation of Omni; Dependence on ENT doctor partnerships; Currency risk in export markets; Scalability of audiologist workforce (15 currently, need to scale with clinic growth)
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, visionary, and disruptive; CEO (ex-Starkey MD) exhibits deep domain expertise; Emphasis on solving systemic access gaps; Repeatedly asserts no competition and global first-mover advantage; Clear focus on long-term market creation over short-term competition
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Earkart is not a competitor to global hearing aid brands—it’s a platform that sells their products too, expanding the overall market; Omni enables newborn hearing screening in 2 minutes, a capability absent in most Indian hospitals; The company’s real moat is not the device but the remote diagnostic-service ecosystem tied to ENT clinics
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

deepdive.thesis: Earkart has disrupted India's hearing care market by deploying its patented Omni platform to bring remote diagnostics and hearing aid fitting to Tier 2/3 cities, achieving 7-8% unit market share with 65-70% gross margins in its SIS model; the company is now scaling to 1,500 clinics and expanding into high-value markets like the U.S. and Australia, where its tech has no direct competition.
